subject.title: session-medic: healed session auto-resumes its stale detached task → multi-session races & livelock (+ high thinking-signature poison rate on high-thinkingDefault Opus agents)

question: After session-medic repairs a session, should OpenClaw resume only the triggering turn, fence all previously detached work pending a fresh trigger, or delegate ownership recovery to the coordinating agent surface?
rationale: The reported race depends on task ownership semantics across sibling sessions, and neither the supplied recovery fixes nor the issue establish a current public contract for cancellation, resumption, or shared-artifact locking.

options.title: Fence detached work after recovery
options.body: Preserve session context but require a fresh coordinator or user trigger before any detached task can resume, with a visible recovery outcome.

options.title: Resume only the active trigger
options.body: Allow the request that caused the recoverable failure to retry, but cancel older queued or detached intent using an explicit run identity boundary.

options.title: Keep current resumption semantics
options.body: Retain automatic continuation and document that multi-agent coordinators must serialize artifact ownership externally.

recommendation.title: Fence detached work after recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve session context but require a fresh coordinator or user trigger before any detached task can resume, with a visible recovery outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged recovery behavior most directly frames the lifecycle boundary that this decision would alter.
